Adult softball league schedule: diamonds, start times and makeup nights

An adult rec softball or kickball league has three jobs: decide who plays whom, decide which diamond and what start time, and cope with the team that has a wedding on week four. A round robin does the first, and the other two are where a hand-made spreadsheet breaks. Six teams on a Tuesday night is a common size: 5 weeks, 3 games a night.

Open the free schedule tool (paste your teams, list diamonds, start times and blackout dates, get dates and a CSV or calendar file)

A worked example: 6 teams, 2 diamonds, 2 start times, one blackout

Six invented teams play a single round robin on Tuesdays from 14 April 2026, with games at 18:30 and 20:00 on two diamonds. Walk-Offs cannot play on 5 May. Home team is listed first.

RoundDateGames (diamond and time)
Round 1Tue 14 Apr 2026Grand Slammers v Foul Ballers (Diamond 2 18:30), Bat Pack v Walk-Offs (Diamond 1 20:00), Dugout Dogs v Pitch Perfect (Diamond 2 20:00)
Round 2Tue 21 Apr 2026Pitch Perfect v Grand Slammers (Diamond 1 18:30), Walk-Offs v Dugout Dogs (Diamond 2 18:30), Foul Ballers v Bat Pack (Diamond 2 20:00)
Round 3Tue 28 Apr 2026Foul Ballers v Walk-Offs (Diamond 1 18:30), Bat Pack v Pitch Perfect (Diamond 2 18:30), Grand Slammers v Dugout Dogs (Diamond 1 20:00)
Round 4Tue 5 May 2026Dugout Dogs v Bat Pack (Diamond 1 18:30), Pitch Perfect v Foul Ballers (Diamond 1 20:00)
Round 5Tue 12 May 2026Foul Ballers v Dugout Dogs (Diamond 1 18:30), Bat Pack v Grand Slammers (Diamond 2 18:30), Pitch Perfect v Walk-Offs (Diamond 2 20:00)
Makeup 1Tue 19 May 2026Walk-Offs v Grand Slammers (Diamond 1 20:00)

Every team plays every other team once and no diamond is used twice at the same start. On 5 May Walk-Offs is out, so only two games are played, and its one missed game against Grand Slammers is the makeup on 19 May. The slot assignment is a seeded search, so the same input always gives the same table.

Questions

How do you make an adult softball league schedule?

List the teams, pick the weeknight, and use a round robin so every team plays every other team once. Six teams play 5 rounds of 3 games. Then give each game a diamond and a start time so no diamond is booked twice.

What if a team cannot play on one night?

Enter the team and the date as a blackout. That team is left out of that night's round, and the one game it misses moves to a makeup night at the end of the season, so nothing else in the schedule changes.

How many diamonds does a six-team league need?

Three games a night need three diamond-and-start-time slots: two diamonds at two start times give four, which leaves one spare slot and lets the tool spread early and late starts fairly.

How do you keep the 18:30 and 20:00 starts fair?

Count how many early starts each team gets over the season and keep the counts within one of each other, so the same team is not always stuck with the late game after work.

What if a game is rained out?

Move it with the rainout box: the game goes to the earliest later night both teams are free and a diamond is open, and nothing else in the schedule moves.

Chess club round robin schedule for seven players: boards, byes and pairings

A club ladder or ratings-free round robin is the simplest fair format for a chess club: everyone plays everyone once, nobody is knocked out, and the final table needs no tie-break tournament. The snag is the odd number. Seven players means one person sits out each week, and the organiser has to make sure it is a different person each time. This guide works one season through: 7 players, Monday evenings, 3 boards, 7 weeks.

Open the free schedule tool (paste your teams, pick the night, get dates and a CSV or calendar file)

A worked example: 7 players, 3 boards, one bye each

Seven invented players meet on Monday evenings from 14 September 2026, all games starting at 19:00 on Board 1, 2 or 3. Seven players give 3 games and a bye a week. The player listed first in a game has White.

RoundNightGames
Round 1Mon 14 Sep 2026Ben v Gus (Board 1), Finn v Chloe (Board 2), Dev v Ella (Board 3); bye: Ana
Round 2Mon 21 Sep 2026Chloe v Ana (Board 1), Gus v Dev (Board 2), Ella v Finn (Board 3); bye: Ben
Round 3Mon 28 Sep 2026Dev v Ben (Board 1), Ana v Ella (Board 2), Finn v Gus (Board 3); bye: Chloe
Round 4Mon 5 Oct 2026Ella v Chloe (Board 1), Ben v Finn (Board 2), Gus v Ana (Board 3); bye: Dev
Round 5Mon 12 Oct 2026Finn v Dev (Board 1), Chloe v Gus (Board 2), Ana v Ben (Board 3); bye: Ella
Round 6Mon 19 Oct 2026Gus v Ella (Board 1), Dev v Ana (Board 2), Ben v Chloe (Board 3); bye: Finn
Round 7Mon 26 Oct 2026Ana v Finn (Board 1), Ella v Ben (Board 2), Chloe v Dev (Board 3); bye: Gus

That is 21 games over 7 weeks, every pair meets exactly once, and each player sits out exactly one week. White and Black are shared out so that every player has White three times and Black three times, with one bye.

Questions

How do you make a round robin for seven chess players?

List the seven players, pick the club night and give the number of boards. With an odd number of players one is paired with nobody each week, so the tool plays seven weeks of three games and gives every player exactly one bye.

How many weeks does a chess club round robin take?

For an odd number of players it takes as many weeks as there are players, so seven players need seven weeks. For an even number it takes one week fewer than the number of players.

Who gets White in a round robin?

The tool alternates colours so each player has White and Black the same number of times, give or take one. In the seven-player example everyone has three games with White and three with Black.

What if a player cannot come one week?

Add the player and the date under blackout dates. Only that game moves to a makeup night after the main rounds, and the rest of the evening goes ahead.

How do you rank a chess club round robin?

Score 1 for a win, one half for a draw and 0 for a loss. In the tool you can use 2-1-0 points and break ties on head-to-head results, and type the results in to see the standings update.

Cornhole league schedule: lanes, start times and holiday weeks

Bar and backyard cornhole leagues run on a few boards and a few start times, and the weeks around a holiday are always short. A round robin settles who plays whom; the lanes, start times and skipped nights settle when. This guide works one season through.

How do you make a cornhole league schedule?

List the teams, pick the weeknight, list the lanes and start times, and add any nights the bar or park is unavailable as skip dates. The tool plays a round robin so every team meets every other team once, and gives each game a lane and start time.

How many lanes does an 8-team cornhole league need?

Eight teams play 4 games a round. Two lanes at two start times (18:30 and 19:30) give exactly four slots, so every team plays once each night.

What happens on a holiday week with no play?

Add the date as a skip date. The season simply runs on the following Wednesday. In the example 1 July is skipped, so Round 5 is on 8 July and no game is lost.

Does an 8-team cornhole league need byes?

No. An even number of teams all play every round. With seven or nine teams one team sits out each round.

Darts league fixtures: a home-and-away schedule for a six-team pub league

A pub darts league is a double round robin: every team plays every other team twice, once on its own board and once on the opponent's. The job for the captain or league secretary is making sure each team hosts as often as it travels, nobody has a run of away nights, and every pair meets exactly twice. Doing it on a spreadsheet takes an evening and the first mistake usually shows up in week four. This guide works one season through: 6 pub teams, Thursdays, 10 weeks.

Open the free schedule tool (paste your teams, pick the night, get dates and a CSV or calendar file)

A worked example: 6 pubs, double round robin, Thursday nights

Six invented pub teams play from 10 September 2026. The home team, listed first, hosts the match on its own board. Six teams give 3 matches a night, and a double round robin is 10 nights.

Round 2Thu 17 Sep 2026Royal Oak v Red Lion, White Hart v Kings Arms, Crown v Black Horse
Round 3Thu 24 Sep 2026Red Lion v Crown, Royal Oak v White Hart, Black Horse v Kings Arms
Round 4Thu 1 Oct 2026White Hart v Black Horse, Crown v Royal Oak, Kings Arms v Red Lion
Round 5Thu 8 Oct 2026Crown v White Hart, Red Lion v Black Horse, Royal Oak v Kings Arms

That is 30 matches, 15 pairs each meeting twice, and every team hosts 5 times and travels 5 times. The second half mirrors the first, so the two meetings of a pair are always exactly five weeks apart.

Questions

How do you make a darts league fixture list?

List the teams, pick the league night, and tick double round robin. The tool plays every team against every other once in the first half of the season and again in the second half with the venues swapped, with the home team shown first.

How many weeks does a six-team darts league last?

A double round robin of six teams takes 10 weeks, because each team plays the other five twice. Add makeup nights for blackout dates and rainouts, or end-of-season finals, on top.

How do you keep home and away fair in a darts league?

Each pair meets once at each team's board, so every team in the six-team example hosts 5 matches and travels for 5. The tool counts home and away per team and the longest home or away run, so you can see it before you send the fixtures.

What if a pub cannot host on some night?

Add the team and the date under blackout dates. Only the match that clashes moves to a makeup night; the rest of the night goes ahead. Two pubs that share a premises can be listed as sharing a ground so they are not both at home on the same night.

Can I send each team only its own fixtures?

Yes. The per-team download gives every captain a list of its own dates, opponents and home or away, and the calendar export puts them in a phone calendar.

Questions

How long does a round robin tournament take?

Count the match slots, then multiply by the length of one slot. Six teams play 15 games; on 2 courts that is 5 rounds of 2 slots, so 10 slots, or 10 hours at 60 minutes a slot and 7.5 hours at 45. The table gives the slot count for 4 to 16 teams on 1 to 4 courts.

How many courts do I need to finish a round robin in one day?

Divide the slot count by the number of slots you can fit in the day. With 8-hour days of 60-minute slots, 8 teams need 28 slots on 1 court (too long), 14 on 2, 7 on 4. Adding courts helps until a round fits in one slot, which takes half the teams in courts; after that more courts change nothing.

Why is the slot count sometimes higher than games divided by courts?

Each round is played to completion before the next starts, as in the generator, so a round of 3 games on 2 courts takes 2 slots with one court idle in the second. That keeps the schedule easy to run and every team resting between rounds; a looser packing can save a slot or two but lets teams play back to back.

How to assign referees to a league schedule fairly

Once the fixtures exist, someone still has to cover them. Spreadsheets handle this badly: the same two volunteers end up on every Tuesday, a player's own team gets their friend, and nobody notices two games at 7pm sharing one referee until the night. The rules are simple enough to automate, so here they are.

Open the free schedule maker (step 6, Referees and officials)

The rules

  • Every match gets exactly one official.
  • An official never works a match involving their own team.
  • An official is on at most one match per time slot of a night.
  • An official only works the weekdays you list for them, and no more than their cap.
  • Among everyone who qualifies, the least-loaded official takes the match; ties go to whoever has seen these two teams least, then to list order.

A worked example: 4 teams, 3 officials

Teams Hawks, Owls, Wolves and Lynx play a single round robin from Tuesday 6 October 2026. Officials, one per line:

Pat (Hawks)
Sam
Lee: Tue max 2

Pat belongs to Hawks, Sam is free any night, and Lee works Tuesdays only and at most twice.

RoundMatchOfficial
1Hawks v LynxSam
1Owls v WolvesPat
2Lynx v OwlsLee
2Wolves v HawksSam
3Wolves v LynxPat
3Hawks v OwlsLee

Six matches, three officials, two each. Pat never appears on a Hawks game, and no one is on both matches of a round at the same time. A separate test recomputes this table from the same code the tool runs.

Assign your own officials

Questions

How do you assign referees fairly in a league?

Give every match one official and hand each match to whoever has worked the fewest so far. Break ties by who has seen the two teams least, then by list order. That keeps the counts within one of each other without anyone keeping a tally by hand.

Can a referee work a match involving their own team?

Not under these rules. If you put a team in brackets after an official's name, the tool never gives them that team's matches. It also never puts one official on two matches that start at the same time.

What if nobody is free for a match?

The tool leaves that match without an official and lists it with the reason, such as every official being off that weekday or at their match cap, so you can recruit someone or lift a cap.

Can each referee get their own calendar?

Yes. After officials are assigned you can download a calendar file or copy a ready-to-paste note for each official with only the matches they work.

How to balance home and away games in a round robin, with a worked example

In a fair round robin every team plays everyone else once, and the home games and away games are shared as evenly as the number of teams allows. The thing to avoid is a run of two or more home games or two or more away games for the same team. That run is called a break, and the circle method keeps the total as low as it can be.

Open the free schedule tool (paste the teams; home and away are balanced for you)

A worked example: 6 teams, 5 rounds

Six invented teams play a single round robin. Each row is one team's season, one letter per round: H for a home game, A for away. Two of the same letter side by side is a break.

TeamRounds 1 to 5Breaks
HawksH A H A H0
OwlsH A A H A1
FoxesA H H A H1
BearsH A H A A1
LynxA H A H H1
WolvesA H A H A0

Each team plays 5 games, 2 or 3 of them at home. The league has 4 breaks in total, which is the minimum for 6 teams, and no team has more than one. The pattern comes from the same code the page runs and a test recomputes this table from it, so it cannot drift from the tool.

Build your own schedule

Questions

What is a home/away break in a round robin?

A break is two home games or two away games in a row for the same team. Fewer breaks means a fairer season, because long runs at home or away skew results and travel.

What is the fewest breaks a round robin can have?

With an even number of teams n, at least n − 2 breaks across the whole league, and the circle method reaches that: 4 breaks for 6 teams, 6 for 8. With an odd number of teams it can be done with none, because every team has a bye that resets its run.

Does a double round robin have more breaks?

If you simply replay the first half with home and away swapped, yes: the two halves meet at the seam, and an even league ends up with 3 × (n − 2) breaks in total (12 for 6 teams) with at most 3 on one team. Check the seam, where a team that finished the first half away starts the second half away too.

Can I avoid home/away breaks completely?

Not with an even number of teams in a single round robin: n − 2 is the proven minimum. You can only choose which teams carry the breaks, so give them to the teams that mind least rather than leaving it to chance.

How do I check my own schedule for breaks?

Write each team's season as a string of H and A, one letter per round, and look for two matching letters side by side. The free tool does this for you and names any team with three or more home or away games in a row.

How to break ties in league standings, with a worked example

Two teams finish level on points and the trophy, a play-off place or relegation depends on which is ranked higher. If the rule is not written down before the season, the argument starts after the last game. This page shows the usual order and a four-team season where the choice of rule changes the table.

Open the free league tool (type results into the standings box and tick head-to-head)

The usual order

  1. Points (win 3, draw 1, loss 0 unless your league says otherwise), after any deduction or bonus.
  2. Head-to-head among the tied teams only: points, then goal difference, then goals scored in those matches.
  3. Goal difference over the whole season.
  4. Goals scored over the whole season.
  5. A coin toss, a play-off or a draw, decided in advance.

Some leagues put overall goal difference before head-to-head. Both are legitimate; choose one, publish it and keep it.

A worked example

Four invented teams, six matches played:

MatchScore
Owls v Lynx0 - 1
Owls v Hawks6 - 0
Owls v Otters1 - 0
Lynx v Hawks0 - 1
Lynx v Otters1 - 0
Hawks v Otters0 - 0

Owls and Lynx both have 6 points. Ranked by overall goal difference, Owls (+6) are first and Lynx (+1) second. Ranked head-to-head, Lynx are first, because they won the one match between the two:

RankOverall goal difference firstHead-to-head first
1OwlsLynx
2LynxOwls
3HawksHawks
4OttersOtters

The six-goal win over Hawks is why Owls lead on goal difference, but it says nothing about how Owls did against Lynx. Pick the rule that matches how your league wants to reward results.

Rank your own league

Questions

How do you break a tie in league standings?

Pick the order before the season and publish it. The usual order is points, then head-to-head (points, then goal difference, among only the tied teams), then overall goal difference, then goals scored, then a coin toss or play-off. The tool applies exactly this order when you tick head-to-head.

What is the difference between head-to-head and goal difference?

Goal difference counts every match a team played, including big wins over weak teams. Head-to-head counts only the matches between the teams that are level, so it answers who was better when they met.

What if three teams are level on points?

Head-to-head is worked out as a mini-table of only the matches among those three teams. Do not compare two of them by their single meeting and ignore the third; use the mini-table's points, then goal difference, then goals scored.

Can I deduct points and still break ties?

Yes. A deduction or bonus is added to the team's table points first, then every tie-break runs on the adjusted points. In the tool write a line such as Owls -3 pts (late fee) in the results box.

How to make a fantasy football schedule: 12 teams, 14 weeks

Most fantasy leagues have more regular-season weeks than a single round robin needs. Twelve teams meet everyone once in 11 weeks, which leaves 3 weeks over. The fair way to fill them is to keep the round robin intact and repeat a few early weeks, so every team has the same opponents except for the same 3 rematches.

Make my league schedule (paste your team names, pick the weekday, tick double round robin, set Rounds to play to 14)

A worked example: 12 teams, 14 weeks

Teams: Ace, Bolt, Colt, Dash, Echo, Fox, Gale, Hawk, Iris, Jinx, Kite, Lynx. Settings: double round robin, Rounds to play 14, Thursday weeks. The tool plays the 11 weeks of a full round robin and then replays weeks 1 to 3 with home and away swapped (home and away do not matter in fantasy; the tool still keeps them even).

WeeksWhat happensGames per team
1 to 11Every team meets each of the other 11 teams once11
12 to 14Weeks 1 to 3 are repeated3
Total66 different pairings, 18 of them played twice14

Each team has exactly 3 rematches, and the shortest gap between a pair's two games is 11 weeks. A separate test rebuilds this schedule from the same code the tool runs and checks every number above.

Build yours

Questions

How do you make a fantasy football schedule for 12 teams and 14 weeks?

Play one full round robin first: 12 teams need 11 weeks so everyone meets everyone once. Then fill weeks 12 to 14 by repeating the pairings of weeks 1 to 3. Every team ends with 14 games, 11 different opponents and exactly 3 rematches, and no team plays two games in a week.

Why not just pick random opponents each week?

Random draws let one team face the league's best three times and another face the worst, and nothing stops a pair meeting four times. A round robin makes the opponents equal for everyone; only the 3 repeat weeks differ, and they are the same rounds for every team.

Which weeks should the repeat games fall in?

Repeating the first rounds in the last weeks keeps the gap between a rematch and its first meeting at 11 weeks, the longest possible with this plan, so rematches do not feel back to back. Another common choice is to repeat divisional or rival pairings, which this tool leaves to you.

Does it work for 10 or 14 teams?

Yes. Enter the team names, pick the weekday, tick double round robin and set Rounds to play to your regular-season weeks. A 10-team league with 13 weeks gets 9 unique opponents and 4 rematches; a 14-team league with 13 weeks is just 13 games, a single round robin.

How to make a round-robin schedule, with a worked example

A round robin is the simplest fair league: every team plays every other team the same number of times. The hard part is not the pairing, it is everything around it: the odd team who sits out each week, who is at home, which court, and the team captain who cannot play on the 20th.

Open the free schedule generator

A worked example

Five invented pickleball teams play on Tuesday evenings from 6 October 2026 on two courts. Five teams means five rounds of two matches, and each team has one bye. The home team is listed first.

RoundDateCourt 1Court 2Bye
16 OctBolts v EaglesDinks v CometsAces
213 OctComets v AcesEagles v DinksBolts
320 OctDinks v BoltsAces v EaglesComets
427 OctEagles v CometsBolts v AcesDinks
53 NovAces v DinksComets v BoltsEagles

Every pair meets once (ten matches), every team hosts twice and visits twice, nobody has two home or two away games in a row, and each team plays twice on each court. The generator checks all of that with a separate validator before it shows you the result. Bring a blackout date, for example Comets away on 20 October, and only the one match that clashes moves, to a makeup round on the next free Tuesday.

Make your own schedule

Questions

What is a round-robin schedule?

A format where every team plays every other team the same number of times. A single round robin with n teams has n(n-1)/2 matches; a double round robin plays each pair twice, once at each team's home venue. It is the fairest way to rank a small league because nobody is knocked out and the table is decided by everyone's results against everyone.

What happens with an odd number of teams?

The circle method adds an invisible extra team, so each round one real team has a bye. Five teams play five rounds and every team sits out exactly once. The generator lists the bye in each round so the team knows it is not playing that week.

How do you keep home and away fair?

In the circle method the home side of each pairing is set while the rounds are built, not patched afterwards. With an even number of teams the minimum possible number of home or away breaks (two consecutive home games or two consecutive away games) is the number of teams minus two, and the generator reaches it. With an odd number of teams no team gets two home or two away games in a row. A double round robin is mirrored, so every pair plays once at each home.

What if a team cannot play on a certain date?

Type the team and the date as a blackout. The generator moves only the affected match out of that round and plays it in a makeup round after the regular season, so the other teams are not held up. If a date has to be given up entirely, it says so. Check the makeup dates with the teams before you publish.

How to reschedule a rained-out league game, with a worked example

A field is under water on a Tuesday and one match has to move. The wrong fix is to rebuild the season, because every team then has new dates to check. The right fix moves only the cancelled match and leaves the rest. This page shows the rule and a four-team season where the obvious next night is not free.

Open the free league tool (build the schedule, then type the rainout into the rainouts box)

The rule

  1. Take out only the cancelled match, or every match that night if the whole night is off.
  2. Look at each later playing night in order. Skip it if either team already plays, or has a blackout date, that night, or if a skip date such as a holiday falls on it.
  3. On the first night that works, put the match on a free court and time slot, honouring any time limit a team has.
  4. Keep the original home and away, and leave every other fixture exactly where it was.

A worked example

Four invented teams, two courts, Tuesdays at 19:00, starting 6 October 2026. The original schedule:

NightMatches
2026-10-06Owls v Otters (Court 1), Lynx v Hawks (Court 2)
2026-10-13Otters v Lynx (Court 1), Hawks v Owls (Court 2)
2026-10-20Hawks v Otters (Court 1), Owls v Lynx (Court 2)

Hawks v Owls on 13 October is rained out. Owls already play Lynx on 20 October, so that night is not free for them. The match goes to the next Tuesday, 27 October, still on Court 2 at 19:00 with Hawks at home:

NightMatches
2026-10-06Owls v Otters (Court 1), Lynx v Hawks (Court 2)
2026-10-13Otters v Lynx (Court 1)
2026-10-20Hawks v Otters (Court 1), Owls v Lynx (Court 2)
2026-10-27Hawks v Owls (Court 2)

Nobody else's fixtures changed, so only Hawks and Owls have a new date to tell their players.

Reschedule your own league

Questions

What do you do when a league game is rained out?

Move only the cancelled match to the earliest later night when both teams are free and a court is open, and leave every other fixture alone. Moving the whole schedule makes every team re-plan its season for one lost night.

What if a team already plays on the next night?

A team cannot play twice on one night, so the match skips that date and goes to the first later night where both teams are free of games and blackout dates. In the example below, Owls play on 20 October already, so the makeup lands on 27 October.

Should a postponed match change who is home?

No. Keep the original home and away so the season's balance of home and away games does not shift because of the weather.

How do I reschedule a rainout in the tool?

Type the date, then the team names, in the rainouts box, for example 2026-10-13 Owls. Leave the team names off to cancel every match that night. The tool lists each move and keeps the rest of the schedule exactly as it was.

How to run a double-elimination tournament: winners bracket, losers bracket and the reset

In double elimination a team is out only after its second loss. That makes it fairer than single elimination for tournaments where teams travelled and one bad game should not end the weekend. The price is roughly twice the games.

Open the free bracket builder (set the play-off to double elimination on the page)

A worked example: 6 teams, 10 games

Six invented teams are seeded 1 to 6. The bracket is sized to 8, so the #1 and #2 seeds get a first-round bye. Teams that lose in the winners bracket drop into the losers bracket; a second loss ends their run. Matches are named so you can follow who plays whom: "winner of W2M1" is whoever wins that game.

Winners QuarterfinalsW1M4#3 Foxes vs #6 Wolves

Losers round 2 (WB drop-downs)L2M2loser of W1M4 vs loser of W2M1
Losers round 3L3M1winner of L2M1 vs winner of L2M2
Losers round 4 (WB drop-downs)L4M1winner of L3M1 vs loser of W3M1
Grand finalGF1winner of W3M1 vs winner of L4M1

If the losers-bracket team wins GF1, a reset game GF2 is played between the same two teams, which makes 11 games. Otherwise the tournament ends after GF1.

Questions

How many games is a double-elimination tournament?

With 6 teams it is 10 games, or 11 if the grand final reset is needed. In general a double-elimination field of n teams plays between 2n - 2 and 2n - 1 games, because every team except the champion loses exactly twice and the reset game is played only when the losers-bracket team wins the grand final.

What is a grand final reset?

The winners-bracket finalist has not lost yet, the losers-bracket finalist has lost once. If the losers-bracket team wins the grand final, both teams now have one loss, so a second game decides the title. If the winners-bracket team wins the first game, the tournament is over.

How do byes work when the field is not a power of two?

The bracket is sized up to the next power of two (8 for 6 teams) and the top seeds skip the first round. In the example, the #1 and #2 seeds have a first-round bye, and the losers bracket skips every match a bye leaves without an opponent.

When should I use double elimination instead of single?

Use it when one bad game should not end a team's weekend, such as a youth or rec tournament where every team travelled. It costs about twice the games of a single-elimination bracket, so check you have the courts and daylight for them.

How to run a ladder league: challenges and moving up

A ladder is a ranking that plays itself. Everyone starts on a rung. You challenge someone a few rungs above you, and if you win you take their place. Clubs use it for tennis, pickleball, squash, table tennis and darts because nobody needs a fixed fixture list: players arrange their own matches and the ranking is always current.

Open the free ladder (the Ladder card on the page: enter players in rank order, then paste results)

A worked example: 6 players, reach of 2

Start order: Ana, Ben, Cy, Dee, Eli, Fay. Results, oldest first:

Cy beat Ana
Eli beat Cy
Fay beat Dee
RungAfter 3 results
1Eli
2Cy
3Ana
4Ben
5Fay
6Dee

Cy (3rd) beat Ana (1st) and took rung 1, so Ana and Ben each dropped a place. Eli (5th) then beat Cy, who now held rung 1, so Eli takes rung 1 and Cy, Ana, Ben and Dee each drop one. Fay (6th) beat Dee, who had slipped to 5th, and swaps up into that rung. Eli's win was 4 rungs up, beyond a reach of 2, so the tool applies it but lists it for you to overrule. A separate test recomputes this table from the same code the tool runs.

Run your own ladder

Questions

How does a ladder league work?

Players are ranked on rungs. You challenge someone a few rungs above you, play one match, and if you win you take their rung while they and everyone between drop one place. If the higher-ranked player wins, nothing changes. There is no fixed schedule, so it suits clubs where players arrange their own matches.

How many rungs up can you challenge?

Most clubs allow two or three rungs. The tool defaults to three, shows who each player can challenge now, and flags any result beyond the limit so the organiser can overrule it. You can also set it higher.

What is the difference between insert and swap?

Insert, the usual rule, puts the winner on the loser's rung and moves everyone in between down one. Swap only trades the two players' places. Swap is gentler on the players between but lets a player leapfrog slowly.

Is a ladder the same as a round robin?

No. A round robin schedules every pair to meet once. A ladder has no fixed fixtures: the ranking is whatever the results so far say. Use a round robin when you want a fair season, and a ladder when you want an always-open club ranking.

How to run a Mexicano: draw each round from the standings

A Mexicano is a social doubles format for padel, pickleball, badminton and tennis nights. Round one is a random draw. After that, every round is drawn from the table, so players with similar scores end up on the same court and the night gets closer as it goes. Like an Americano, nobody needs a fixed partner and your own points count towards your own total.

Open the free Mexicano draw (the Mexicano card on the page: enter players, courts and finished games)

A worked example: 8 players, 2 courts

Eight invented players on two courts. Round one is a seeded random draw:

How is a Mexicano different from an Americano?

An Americano fixes every pairing in advance so everyone partners as many different people as possible. A Mexicano draws each round after the first from the standings, so players with similar scores meet and the night tightens up as it goes. The tool has both: Build rotation for Americano and Draw next round for Mexicano.

How do you pair a Mexicano round?

Rank the players by points so far and cut the list into groups of four. In each group the top player partners the bottom player against the second and third: 1 & 4 against 2 & 3. If that would repeat a partnership, the tool picks a split that repeats fewer.

Who sits out when the number of players is not a multiple of 4?

Each court needs 4 players, so the extras sit out. The tool sits out whoever has played the most games so far, with a random tie-break, so games stay within one of even.

How do you score a Mexicano?

Each player is credited with the points their side scored in every game, so a strong partner never costs you. Players are ranked by points for, then points difference, then wins. This tool draws the rounds and keeps the table; it is not a rating system.

How to seed and run a single-elimination bracket, with a worked example

Single elimination is the quickest way to find one winner: lose once and you are out. It suits play-offs at the end of a league, one-day pickleball, darts or esports events, and any tournament where courts or daylight are short. The two decisions that go wrong by hand are the seeding order and the byes when the number of teams is not 4, 8 or 16.

Open the free bracket tool (type the teams best seed first; dates continue from your league on the weekdays you choose)

A worked example: 6 teams, 5 games

Six invented teams are seeded 1 to 6. The bracket is sized up to 8 slots, and the two empty slots become byes for the top two seeds, so the #1 and #2 seeds skip the first round. Seeds 1 and 2 are on opposite halves, so they can only meet in the final. "Winner of R1M2" is whoever wins that game.

RoundMatchTeams
QuarterfinalsR1M2#4 Bears vs #5 Lynx
QuarterfinalsR1M4#3 Foxes vs #6 Wolves
SemifinalsR2M1#1 Hawks vs winner of R1M2
SemifinalsR2M2#2 Owls vs winner of R1M4
FinalR3M1winner of R2M1 vs winner of R2M2

The #1 and #2 seeds play only two games to win the title; the other four teams play three. That is the reward for a good league finish, and why seeding should come from standings rather than from who signed up first.

The bracket comes from the same code the page runs and a test recomputes this table from it, so it cannot drift from the tool.

Build your own bracket

Questions

How many games are in a single-elimination tournament?

Always one fewer than the number of teams, whatever the size, because every team except the champion loses exactly once. Six teams play 5 games; sixteen teams play 15.

How does seeding work in a single-elimination bracket?

The bracket is filled so that seed 1 meets the lowest seed, seed 2 the second lowest, and so on, and so that the top seeds can only meet each other late: seeds 1 and 2 are on opposite halves and cannot meet before the final. In an 8-slot bracket the first-round pairings are 1 v 8, 4 v 5, 2 v 7 and 3 v 6.

How do byes work when the number of teams is not a power of two?

The bracket is sized up to the next power of two (8 for 6 teams, 16 for 12) and the empty slots go to the lowest seeds, so the top seeds skip round one. With 6 teams the #1 and #2 seeds have a bye; with 12 teams the top four do.

How many rounds does a single-elimination bracket have?

The base-2 logarithm of the bracket size, rounded up: 3 rounds for 5 to 8 teams, 4 rounds for 9 to 16 teams. A bye does not remove a round; the team just plays its first game in round two.

When is single elimination the wrong choice?

When every team has travelled and expects more than one game, or when seeding is a guess. A round robin or a double-elimination bracket gives each team more games, at the cost of more courts and time.

How to run a Swiss-system tournament, with a worked example

A Swiss tournament is for a club night or a weekend event with more players than there is time for a round robin. Nobody is knocked out, everyone plays every round, and each round pairs people who are doing about equally well. Chess clubs, darts leagues, board-game and card-game events use it.

Open the free pairing tool (it is the Swiss card on the page; pair each round by pasting in the results so far)

A worked example

Six invented players, seeded in the order they signed up. Six players need 3 rounds. Round 1 has no scores yet, so the seed order decides: the top half plays the bottom half.

Round 1WhiteBlack
Board 1AnaDee
Board 2BenEli
Board 3CyFay

Suppose Ana, Ben and Fay win. The three winners now have 1 point and the three losers 0, so round 2 pairs winners with winners and losers with losers, with nobody meeting a previous opponent:

Round 2WhiteBlack
Board 1AnaBen
Board 2FayDee
Board 3EliCy

Fay, on 1 point, plays Dee, on 0, because the other two 1-point players already meet each other: the tool shows that as a "floater" and says so rather than hiding it. Colours alternate, so nobody is white three times running. The pairing is checked by a separate validator before it is shown.

Pair your own round

Questions

How many rounds does a Swiss tournament need?

Enough that one player can be clearly ahead: the next whole number above log base 2 of the player count. Six or eight players need 3 rounds, sixteen need 4. More rounds sort the middle of the table more finely, but the top places are usually settled by this number.

How are players paired in a Swiss round?

Everyone is sorted by score, then players with the same score are paired top half against bottom half, so the strongest of a group meets the weakest of that group. Nobody plays the same opponent twice. In round 1 nobody has a score yet, so the seed order decides.

What happens with an odd number of players?

One player gets a bye each round and is scored as a win. The bye goes to the lowest-ranked player who has not had one yet, so nobody gets two byes before everyone has had one.

How are ties in the standings broken?

By Buchholz: the sum of your opponents' scores. Beating players who went on to do well is worth more than beating players who lost everything. Still level? Sonneborn-Berger is next: the full score of each opponent you beat plus half the score of each you drew, so a win over the leader outweighs a win over the player who lost everything. Players still level after that keep their seed order.

How to run an Americano: rotating partners for padel, pickleball and badminton nights

An Americano is a social doubles format where everyone plays with and against as many different people as possible. Nobody needs a fixed partner, so it suits club nights, open mornings and mixed-level groups. Each round you get a new partner, and your own points count towards your own total.

Eight invented players on two courts play 7 rounds. Everyone plays every round, so there are no sit-outs. Every player partners each of the other seven players exactly once, and nobody plays the same partner twice.

How to schedule a league with limited courts and time slots, with a worked example

A round robin tells you who plays whom each week. It does not tell you which court or what time, and that is where hand-made schedules go wrong: a court booked twice, or one team stuck with the 8 pm slot all season. The rule is simple. Each round has half as many matches as teams (rounded down), and every match needs its own court-and-time slot.

Open the free schedule tool (list your courts and start times; slots are shared out for you)

A worked example: 6 teams, 2 courts, 2 start times

Six invented teams play a single round robin on Tuesdays: 5 rounds of 3 matches. Two courts at 18:00 and 19:00 give four slots a round, one more than needed. Home team is listed first.

RoundMatches (court and time)
1Bears v Foxes (Court A 18:00), Hawks v Wolves (Court A 19:00), Owls v Lynx (Court B 19:00)
2Wolves v Owls (Court A 18:00), Foxes v Hawks (Court B 18:00), Lynx v Bears (Court A 19:00)
3Hawks v Lynx (Court A 18:00), Bears v Owls (Court B 18:00), Foxes v Wolves (Court B 19:00)
4Owls v Hawks (Court A 18:00), Wolves v Bears (Court B 18:00), Lynx v Foxes (Court B 19:00)
5Lynx v Wolves (Court B 18:00), Foxes v Owls (Court A 19:00), Hawks v Bears (Court B 19:00)

Across the five rounds every team plays the 18:00 slot two or three times and the 19:00 slot two or three times, and no court is used twice at the same time. The assignment is a seeded search, so the same input always gives the same table.

Questions

How many courts do I need for a round robin?

Half the number of teams, rounded down, matches per round, so you need that many court-and-time slots in each round. Six teams play 3 matches a round: three courts at one time, or two courts at two times, or one court at three times. Count courts times time slots, not courts alone.

What happens if I do not have enough courts or time slots?

The tool refuses to build the schedule and says how many matches a round needs and how many your courts and times fit, rather than quietly double-booking a court. Add a court, add a time slot, or play fewer teams per night by splitting into pools.

How do I make early and late slots fair?

Count how many early slots each team gets across the season and keep the counts within one of each other. The tool assigns slots by seeded simulated annealing against that cost, so in the six-team example every team plays the 18:00 slot two or three times out of five.

Can a team that can only play early be given early slots?

Yes. Give that team a time limit such as Lob Squad: 17:00 and it is only offered slots that start by then; rainout moves respect the limit and the validator flags any breach.

Why does the same input always give the same schedule?

The slot search is seeded, so the same teams, courts, times and seed give the same schedule every time. Change the seed to get a different, equally valid arrangement.

How to schedule a round robin with an odd number of teams, with a worked example

With 6 or 8 teams everyone plays every round. With 5, 7 or 9 someone has to sit out each round, and doing that by hand usually ends with one team idle twice while another never rests. The fix is the circle method: add an imaginary extra team, schedule as if it were real, and whoever is paired with it has the bye.

Questions

How many rounds does a round robin with an odd number of teams have?

As many as there are teams: 5 teams need 5 rounds, 7 teams need 7. An even number of teams needs one fewer round than teams, because nobody sits out; an odd number adds a dummy team, and whoever is paired with it has the bye.

How many byes does each team get?

Exactly one in a single round robin, whatever the size. With 5 teams that is one idle round each across 5 rounds, with two games played in every round.

How many games are played in total?

n × (n − 1) ÷ 2, odd or even. Five teams play 10 games and seven teams play 21, because each team plays every other team once: 4 games each for 5 teams.

Is a bye fair when teams play on different dates?

Only if the bye falls in a different round for each team, which the circle method guarantees. If a team needs a particular week off, give them the round where they have the bye by choosing which team takes which line of the list before dates are set.

What do I do for a double round robin with an odd number of teams?

Repeat the same rounds with home and away reversed. Each team then has two byes, one in each half, and meets every opponent twice.

Questions

What is a round robin schedule template?

A fixture list for a set number of teams, labelled by team number, in which every team plays every other team once. Replace the numbers with your team names: Team 1 is the first name on your list, Team 2 the second, and so on. Home is listed first.

Why does the 8 team round robin have 7 rounds?

In each round every team plays once, and each team has 7 opponents, so 7 rounds. With 8 teams there are 4 games per round and 28 games in total.

What do I do with an odd number of teams?

One team sits out each round (a bye), so the schedule has as many rounds as teams. The 5, 7, 9 and 11 team tables below show the team with the bye in each round; every team gets exactly one.

Can I use these for a double round robin?

Yes. Play the same rounds again with home and away reversed. The generator does this for you with the double round robin option, and also puts real dates, courts and time slots on the rounds.

How many games are in a single-elimination tournament?

One fewer than the number of teams, because every game eliminates exactly one team and all but the champion go out: 12 teams, 11 games. Byes do not add games.

How many rounds does a bracket with byes have?

The number of rounds is the exponent of the next power of two: 5 to 8 teams is 3 rounds, 9 to 16 is 4, 17 to 32 is 5. The extra slots become first-round byes for the top seeds.

Two fewer than twice the number of teams (12 teams: 22), plus one more game only if the team from the losers bracket wins the grand final and forces the reset.

Volleyball league schedule when the gym is booked: closed dates and makeups

Adult and school-hall volleyball leagues rarely get a gym every week. The second court is taken by a basketball night, the hall is hired out for a fair, a holiday closes the building. A hand-made schedule then has games on nights with no court for them. A round robin fixes who plays whom; the closed-court dates decide when each game can actually be played. This guide works one season through: 6 teams, 2 gyms, Thursdays, and Gym 2 shut on two of them.

Open the free schedule tool (paste your teams, list the gyms and the dates each is closed, get dates and a CSV or calendar file)

A worked example: 6 teams, 2 gyms, 2 start times, 2 closures

Six invented teams play a single round robin on Thursdays from 5 November 2026. Gym 1 and Gym 2 each start games at 19:00 and 20:00, four slots for the 3 matches a round needs. Gym 2 is closed on 19 and 26 November, so those two nights have only two open slots. Home team is listed first.

RoundNightGames (gym and time)

Round 2Thu 12 NovAces v Blockers (Gym 2 19:00), Diggers v Spikers (Gym 1 20:00), Floaters v Setters (Gym 2 20:00)
Round 3Thu 19 NovDiggers v Floaters (Gym 1 19:00), Blockers v Setters (Gym 1 20:00)
Round 4Thu 26 NovFloaters v Blockers (Gym 1 19:00), Aces v Diggers (Gym 1 20:00)

Questions

How do you make a volleyball league schedule when the gym is booked some nights?

List the teams, pick the weeknight, and list each court with the dates it is closed. The tool plays a round robin on the nights you have and moves any game that no open court can hold to a makeup round, so no game lands in a closed gym.

How many gyms does a six-team volleyball league need?

Six teams play 3 matches a round. Two gyms at two start times give four slots, so a night with one gym closed still holds two matches; count gyms times start times, and note which dates drop a gym.

What happens to games on a night a gym is closed?

Only the matches the open courts cannot hold move. In the example Gym 2 is closed on 19 and 26 November, so each of those nights plays 2 of its 3 matches and the third goes to a makeup night at the end of the season.

Does a six-team volleyball league need a bye?

No. An even number of teams all play every round. With five or seven teams one team sits out each round.

How do you tell the teams about a moved game?

Use the per-team message download: each team gets only its own dates, courts and opponents, so a changed night reaches the right captain without a league-wide email.

How do you make a youth soccer league schedule?

List the teams, pick the Saturday, and use a round robin so every team plays every other team once. Nine teams play 9 rounds of 4 matches, and one team has a bye each week. Then give each match a field and a kickoff time so no field is booked twice.

What do you do with an odd number of youth soccer teams?

One team sits out every round. A single round robin of nine teams has 9 rounds, and every team gets exactly one bye, so nobody misses more than one week.

How many fields does a nine-team league need?

Four matches a week need four field-and-kickoff slots: two fields at two kickoff times, or four fields at one. Count fields times kickoff times, not fields alone.

How do you keep the 09:00 and 10:30 kickoffs fair?

Count how many early kickoffs each team gets across the season and keep the counts within one of each other, so the same team is not always the one up at dawn.

What if a Saturday is rained out or a field is closed?

Add the date as a skip date, list the field as closed on that date, or move a rained-out round with the rainout box; the tool keeps every field and kickoff free of clashes.
